title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: Remember, one-hot encoding is a way to represent categorical variables as binary vectors. For the $$job_{type}$$ variable, each category (blue collar, white collar, managerial) is represented by a separate binary column. In this case, if a worker is blue collar, the $$x_b$$ variable will be $$1$$, and the others will be $$0$$.

title: Substitute Known Values
text: For a blue collar worker with $$10$$ years of education, substitute $$x_{edu}$$ with $$10$$ and $$x_b$$ with $$1$$ in the equation. What happens to $$x_m$$?

title: Calculate the Contribution of Education
text: Calculate the contribution of education to the wage using the term $$3x_{edu}$$. What is the result when $$x_{edu}$$ is 10?

title: Calculate the Contribution of Job Type
text: For a blue collar worker, calculate the contribution of the job type using the term $$-3x_b$$. What is the result when $$x_b$$ is 1?

title: Combine the Contributions
text: Now, combine the contributions from education and job type with the intercept $$-8$$. What is the final expression you need to evaluate?
